messages:
Ana L.: Heads-up — we saw a flood of SLO alerts last night that looked like duplicates across multiple routes. Console created separate cards for what seemed to be the same root cause. Can we discuss dedupe + escalation UX?

TJ: Do you have an example? Was it duplicated because of per-route SLOs or multiple downstream errors?

Ana L.: It was the nginx 503 spike -> bubbled into our per-route latency and also the global inference-throughput SLO. Snip of alerts:```
- route:/v1/generate tenant:acme error:503 count:120
- slo:inference-latency route:/v1/generate tenant:acme breach:true
- slo:throughput global tenant:acme breach:true
```
All fired within 30s so console showed 3 separate alert cards.

Mike R.: Yeah that triggers the classic fan-out. Proposal: introduce an ingest-side fingerprint that groups alerts with the same root_keys (service, error_class, tenant_id) and then surface a single card with expandable rows for affected SLOs/routes.

Sarah P.: This sounds good but watch multi-tenant semantics — some customers want per-route visibility for billing/SLAs. We should support both grouping and per-tenant override to opt into "no-grouping" for a tenant or route.

TJ: UX question — default grouped card should show aggregate severity and a primary escalation contact. Expanding shows the per-SLO items (with links to console/trace). That keeps noise down but preserves detail.

Zoe D.: From devex side: we need an API shape that can represent both grouped and ungrouped alerts. Something like:```json
{
  "fingerprint": "sha256(...)",
  "group_keys": ["service","error_class","tenant_id"],
  "members": [ {"slo":"inference-latency","route":"/v1/generate"}, ... ]
}
```
Would require a minor schema bump to alerts ingestion.

Mike R.: Implementation note: dedupe at ingestion by computing fingerprint = hash(group_keys + time_window_bucket). The time-window should be configurable (default 60s or 5m). We also need to support "sticky" grouping for longer incidents so the UI keeps them together while they’re active.

Sarah P.: Agree. Also think about escalation windows: if grouped alert stays active for X minutes escalate to oncall; if only intermittent, suppress invites and send digest. Need config: escalation_after, notify_rate_limit, digest_window.

Ana L.: Can we include a short example of console config? e.g.:```yaml
alert_grouping:
  enabled: true
  group_by: [service, error_class, tenant_id]
  window_seconds: 120
  escalation_after_minutes: 15
  notify_rate_limit_per_tenant_per_hour: 4
  tenant_overrides:
    acme: { grouping: false }
```
Would that cover most cases?

TJ: Yes, that looks reasonable. One more edge: multiple distinct causes that share the same error_class (eg 503 from different CDNs). We need to allow adding more keys (route_prefix, upstream_cluster) and provide a fuzzy grouping toggle.

Mike R.: For the backend: compute fingerprint = H(service||error_class||maybe:upstream_cluster||tenant) then store group state in alerts-store with last_seen timestamp and member list. When last_seen > window + sticky_ttl mark group closed.

alertbot: [incident created] #INC-2026-042: multiple SLO alerts grouped (link: https://incidents/repo/INC-2026-042)

Zoe D.: Next steps: 1) spec + API small PR for group payload, 2) console mock for grouped card + expand, 3) allow tenant override UI, 4) add integration test for rate_limit/digest. I can own the mock + UX writeup. :+1:

TJ: I'll open an engineering RFC and link to this thread. Mike/Sarah can sketch the ingest algorithm.

Ana L.: Awesome — thanks. If we can get a beta in staging with grouping enabled and window=120s that should cut last-night noise by ~80%. :eyes:
